claims.text: missing struct fields like best_height in estimateSmartFee and mismatched integer and enum types lead to serialization bugs and compilation issues
claims.quote: It seems to me the capnp wrapper needs some updates (missing field, 32/64 bit params, param rename, bool vs uint64, enums as unsigned, optional mapping, unused declarations, comments, etc).
claims.status_note: fixed by author in subsequent push
claims.status_by_quote: You found a lot of annoying discrepencies and a real bug in the estimateSmartFee best_height return value, which should all be fixed now.

claims.text: node segfaults if a non-C++ client passes null transaction data or unhandled enum values over IPC
claims.quote: Also what happens here is tx is a null pointer (allowed by capnp spec AFAIU)? I think we will immediately try to deference it in BroadcastTransaction and segfault.
claims.status_note: author replied explaining that capnp allows null/defaults and discussed trade-offs and future mitigations
claims.status_by_quote: This is a legitimate concern, and it's not specific to this method or to these parameters.

claims.text: node aborts with an assertion failure if an IPC client requests getBlockHash for a height exceeding the active chain tip
claims.quote: when we pass the height, which is greater than the current tip, then the node crashes and exits with the error... Assertion `chainman().ActiveChain()[height]' failed. Aborted (core dumped)

claims.text: node could hit undefined behavior when switching on broadcastmethod without safe enum mapping or a default case
claims.quote: broadcastmethod is switched on (e.g. here) with no default case, as is our convention. but we don't check incoming value is mapped to the enum safely.
claims.status_note: author explained C++ callers enforce explicit values, and non-C++ callers must handle omitted values safely
claims.status_by_quote: In C++, the compiler enforces at each call site that explicit values need to be passed for all parameters which don't have defaults.

claims.text: rename descendants parameter to cluster_count post-cluster mempool
claims.quote: even though these are positional, I think we can rename descendants -> cluster_count post-cluster mempool (and as this is public facing).
claims.status_note: author confirmed the parameter was renamed upstream and agreed it should be updated
claims.status_by_quote: Good catch. It looks like the parameter was renamed in commit 957ae232414b38adcf9358e198fded42f7c1feea and this PR was not updated.

claims.text: why not omit ChainClient::start from the exposed interface or throw an exception rather than asserting
claims.quote: Why not omit start from the exposed base interface or make this throw a protocol error instead of asserting.
claims.status_note: author explained libmultiprocess generation requirements and agreed an exception could be thrown instead
claims.status_by_quote: This could throw an exception instead of assert. It shouldn't matter very much because I don't think there's a way this could be accidentally called.

claims.quote: Builds fine without `#include <any>` using `g++` on Linux?
claims.status_note: author confirmed it was leftover and removed it
claims.status_by_quote: Good catch, I think this must have been left over from a previous version of this file. Removed now.

claims.text: parameterize Wrap with any CAddress version to test alternative crypto primitives
claims.quote: i think `Wrap` could be parameterized with any `CAddress` version.
claims.status_note: author explained current hardcoded serialization is simplest but customized formats can be added later
claims.status_by_quote: For now though the easiest thing is for the wrapped stream to just hardcode parameters that serialize all the data.

claims.text: why is custom functionality introduced for findBlock and how to validate changes without tests
claims.quote: why is so much custom functionality introduced for `findBlock`?
claims.status_note: author explained recursive structs require custom capnp translation code
claims.status_by_quote: Chain::findBlock and the handful of other Chain methods taking FoundBlock input/output arguments need custom code because these are converted to FoundBlockParam and FoundBlockResult Cap'n Proto structs to make IPC calls, and these structs are recursive

claims.text: whether UniValue in interfaces is intended to be refactored eventually
claims.quote: Is the intention to eventually refactor this?
claims.status_note: author explained UniValue usage in RPC forwarding, settings, and ban map
claims.status_by_quote: In general there are lots of ways current interfaces are not ideal and can be improved over time

claims.text: whether Data blobs and enums should be strongly typed in capnp for non-C++ clients
claims.quote: More generally I have been wondering if it would be a good idea to eventually strongly type these `Data` blobs (and similarly the enums)?
claims.status_note: author explained tradeoffs of maintenance burden and suggested incremental adoption
claims.status_by_quote: tradeoff is just that defining capnproto structs for all the serialized classes adds more code that will need to be maintained

claims.text: update the PR description to mention the dependency on PR 30509
claims.quote: can you update the description with what you mention in ..., regarding #30509 ?

claims.text: how to build the branch on macOS and whether to use MULTIPROCESS=1 or build libmultiprocess from source

claims.status_by_quote: definitely it should be easiest to just check out this branch and use it as is
